candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — antidotes, adverse effects and evaluation of medication response
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — enoxaparin reversal
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that protamine provides incomplete reversal of enoxaparin and requires continued bleeding and adverse-reaction monitoring.

options.A: Protamine completely neutralizes all enoxaparin anti-factor Xa activity, so further bleeding assessment is unnecessary
options.B: Enoxaparin reversal is incomplete; anti-factor Xa activity may persist, so the nurse must continue assessing bleeding and the client's response while also watching for protamine reactions
options.C: Protamine has no clinically meaningful effect on enoxaparin and therefore should never be used for enoxaparin-associated bleeding
options.D: Once protamine is started, severe hypotension or anaphylactoid reactions are no longer relevant safety concerns

candidate.rationale: Protamine can largely neutralize enoxaparin, but current labeling states that anti-factor Xa activity is never completely neutralized and reaches only about 60% maximal neutralization. Ongoing bleeding assessment remains necessary. Protamine itself can cause severe hypotension and anaphylactoid reactions, so administration requires appropriate monitoring and resuscitation capability.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Protamine incompletely reverses enoxaparin anti-Xa activity and carries important infusion-reaction risk.
candidate.source_locator: Section 10 Overdosage — protamine may largely neutralize enoxaparin; anti-Factor Xa activity never completely neutralized, maximum about 60%; protamine may cause severe hypotensive/anaphylactoid reactions
candidate.stem: A client with serious bleeding after enoxaparin receives protamine sulfate. Which nursing interpretation is most accurate after the protamine is given?
